typography-as-brand-voice.prior: treat type as the primary identity carrier, so distinctive faces and expressive contrast do the branding work themselves

meaning-first-color.prior: Color should encode meaning and identity rather than decorate, so every hue maps to a concept, state, or accent that communicates intent.

airy-minimalism.prior: prioritize open space and lightweight layering so content breathes and feels effortless, unconstrained, and premium

always-in-motion.prior: Signal that the product is alive and present by keeping subtle, self-sustaining motion running in the background, so presence is felt without demanding attention or interaction.

depth-through-light-not-lines.prior: Convey hierarchy and elevation by simulating how light, shadow, and translucency behave in physical space rather than using explicit borders or dividers.

tactile-realism.prior: surfaces should evoke physical material presence so interfaces feel believable and touchable

friction-over-refusal.prior: When a user acts against retention, slow and soften rather than deny—preserve the relationship by adding cost and acknowledgment instead of hard blocks.

friction-over-freedom.prior: When users try to disengage, keep them nominally in control while raising the cost of exit—so retention is preserved without an explicit block.

canvas-centric-layering.prior: anchor everything to one central canvas and layer contextual panels and overlays onto it, so a single spatial frame stays the stable reference point for all information

moves.entity-driven-color: --entity-air: #4da8ff and --entity-ground: #b07bff distinguish subject categories (air vs ground), plus globals.css comment 'entity-driven signal color'; usage color: signal.hue and background: signal.hue bind hue to the entity/signal
moves.semantic-status-color: --signal-live #34e0a1, --signal-warn #ffcf5c, --signal-crit #ff4d6d encode live/warning/critical states; .presence beacon-pulse uses live signal color for presence
moves.expressive-accent: --accent #ff4d1f and --accent-hot #ff7a3d saturated orange; elev-dramatic shadow bleeds accent: 0 24px 64px -16px rgba(255,77,31,0.2); comment 'expressive type on a dark ground'
moves.restrained-neutral-chrome: deep neutral ground/surface ramp (--ground #080b12 through --surface-2 #1b2233, --edge #232c40) and text ramp text-hi/mid/dim ground the chrome; focal object uses NEUTRAL ink shadow with 'hue lives on marking'

application.evidence: --ground:#080b12 painted on body background and page canvas — the base dark ground
--surface-0/1/2 stack the lit focal object (gradient 1b2233→0d1119) and DetailPanel background:var(--surface-2)
--text-hi/mid/dim carry all copy across BeaconCanvas, BeaconCard, DetailPanel
--edge:#232c40 for borders/dividers, e.g. DetailPanel border:1px solid var(--edge)
neutral ink drives the dramatic float shadow and bevel — 'NEUTRAL ink (hue lives on marking)', repeating-linear texture, glass rgba(13,17,25,0.72)
--accent:#ff4d1f used as focal marking color in BeaconCanvas (color:var(--accent)) and page.tsx (background:var(--accent)) — the lit focal signal
accent glow in elevation: elev-dramatic box-shadow rgba(255,77,31,0.2)
--signal-live/warn/crit surface only as signal.hue on BeaconCard fill/text and DetailPanel status marking — status encoding only
--entity-air/--entity-ground category hues reserved to encode beacon entity type in data

components.instantiate: Build a component that opens as a layer over the canvas, carrying material [lighting, sheen] and hosting interaction [demote-not-remove, interaction-lock, manufactured-latency, motion-ack, multi-phase] and embodying the pattern(s) 'spotlight-filter' (selecting one member of a collection spotlights it while the rest demote (fade/dim) in place) — combine the aesthetic and the interaction in the SAME object.

Build a component that expands attached to its trigger (a dropdown/disclosure), carrying material [bevel, lighting, sheen, texture] and hosting interaction [demote-not-remove, interaction-lock, manufactured-latency, multi-phase] — combine the aesthetic and the interaction in the SAME object.
On drag, it builds a component that sits inline, hosting interaction [demote-not-remove, interaction-lock, motion-ack, reactive-continuous, spring-physics] Triggered by drag.

_checklist: COMPOSITION — organize around a central-canvas spine.  WHY: anchor everything to one central canvas and layer contextual panels and overlays onto it.

TYPOGRAPHY — carry the moves ['custom-display-face', 'distinct-body-face', 'expressive-weight', 'extreme-scale-contrast', 'treated-microtype', 'type-as-graphic'] · DEPLOYMENT: reserve ['custom-display-face', 'expressive-weight', 'extreme-scale-contrast', 'treated-microtype', 'type-as-graphic'] for the focal moments — the source deploys sparingly ('custom-display-face' in ~20% of source files, 'expressive-weight' in ~20% of source files, 'extreme-scale-contrast' in ~20% of source files, 'treated-microtype' in ~20% of source files, 'type-as-graphic' in ~20% of source files); a reserved move applied everywhere stops reading as identity. WHY: Color should encode meaning and identity rather than decorate.

_guide.deployment_frequency: An identity move has a HOME. Carrying a move does NOT mean maximizing it: the source deploys its strongest moves — textures, glows, loops, display type — at a specific frequency (the checklist's DEPLOYMENT notes give the observed rate), and that restraint is itself part of the identity. Applying a reserved move to every element destroys the figure/ground contrast that makes it read as identity; the build goes noisy and one-dimensional, and the gate flags clear over-application. Match the deployment pattern, not just the move.
_guide.build_to_the_why: The checklist's WHY clauses are the product's dispositions — its soul. Build to those principles, not just to pass the checks. A check is a floor, not the finish: passing conformance means you didn't violate the grammar, NOT that it feels like one designer's hand.
build_order: 1. SKELETON — stand up the composition spine and the focal object first (structure before style). A great skin on no spine reads as generic.
2. MATERIAL — give the focal object its layered material (the SURFACE moves).
3. BEHAVIOR — bind the interaction grammar (gesture → response) on the component roles.
4. STYLE — carry each facet's moves at the stated MAGNITUDE (as loud as the source, not a tasteful echo).
5. POLISH — the craft below. This is where a passing build becomes a good one.

you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.note: Static analysis reads declared DOM/CSS, not the rendered/animated result. These are real identity but UNVERIFIABLE — a green report does NOT cover them, so they are yours to get right by hand.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.motion_smoothness: Real easing and staged timing — no linear tweens, no jank. Animate transform/opacity, not layout. Honor prefers-reduced-motion.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.color_harmony: The palette must read as ONE system — even lightness/chroma steps, restrained hue families. Passing the color moves ≠ a harmonious palette.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.type_layout: Clean arrangement — aligned to a grid, consistent vertical rhythm, a hierarchy that reads. (Rich size vocabularies are fine; sloppy ARRANGEMENT is not.)
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.material_feel: Glossy vs flat, focal richness — the rendered richness the layer/alpha counts can't distinguish. Make the focal object look genuinely lit.

_guide.reading_the_gate: The gate is DETERMINISTIC except color, which is semantic (marking-vs-decoration is a judgment about meaning). Consequences: (a) a FAIL that stays IDENTICAL on UNCHANGED code is REAL — fix the build, do not re-run hoping it clears, and do not contort code to game a signature. (b) The color check can shift between edits because it re-reads meaning; trust a stable verdict on unchanged code. (c) 'accent decorates instead of marks' is about MEANING: a colored glow on a data entity MARKS (good); a decorative gradient DECORATES (flagged).
